summary: SteerVAD proposes a tuning-free video anomaly detection framework that identifies discriminative attention heads (LAEs) via a Fisher-discriminant-style scatter ratio and dynamically re-scales their features through a lightweight hierarchical meta-controller. The geometric framing is interesting and the data-efficiency story is compelling. However, the performance margins over the closest tuning-free competitor are very small (≤0.87 pp) and statistically unvalidated, the method is tested on only two datasets with a single MLLM backbone, and several claims—notably about 'narrowing the gap' with fine-tuned methods—are not supported by the XD-Violence numbers. Substantial additional experiments are needed before the contribution is commensurate with an ICLR paper.
strengths: The paradigm shift from passive feature reading to active geometric intervention is a clean, well-motivated conceptual contribution that unifies a set of algorithmic choices (LAE identification + HMC) under one coherent framework.

The calibration stability experiment (Table 3, 10 independent seeds, identical LAE sets, σ≈0.04% AUC) is rigorous and builds genuine confidence that the RSA-identified circuits reflect intrinsic model properties rather than calibration-set artifacts.
The ablation study (Table 2) isolates each HMC component (GSG, LGM, steering type) and the RSA selection strategy with clear controls, yielding interpretable incremental performance improvements.
Training on ≤1% of labeled data while remaining competitive with methods trained on the full set is a practically valuable result for low-resource deployment scenarios.

The composite training objective (BCE + L2 sparsity on sglobal for normal samples) is well-motivated and grounded: it explicitly discourages false-positive activations rather than relying solely on class loss.

key_concerns.issue: Statistically unsupported performance margins. The main result (Table 1) reports only point estimates. The closest tuning-free competitor, HiProbeVAD, trails by 0.43 pp AUC on UCF-Crime and 0.87 pp AP on XD-Violence. Table 3 reports intra-method AUC variance of ±0.04% across seeds, but cross-method variance (due to different implementation choices, pre-processing, etc.) is almost certainly larger. Without confidence intervals or significance tests, the claim of superior performance over HiProbeVAD is not established.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean ± std over at least 5 seeds for all methods the authors re-ran, or clearly note which baselines use published numbers. Conduct a paired significance test (e.g., bootstrap AUC test or Wilcoxon on frame-level scores) against the two nearest tuning-free methods.

key_concerns.issue: Single backbone generalization gap. All experiments use InternVL3 exclusively. The entire contribution—RSA head selection, HMC conditioning, anisotropic scaling—is evaluated on one architecture. It is unknown whether the identified LAE circuits (L18H4, L23H24, L21H21, L22H7) are architecture-specific quirks or a general phenomenon, and whether the HMC design is robust to different hidden-state dimensions and attention configurations.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Include at least one additional frozen MLLM backbone (e.g., LLaVA-1.5 or Qwen-VL) to validate generality. Even a single additional result on one dataset would significantly strengthen the generalizability claim.

key_concerns.issue: HiProbeVAD is a self-reference whose anonymization obscures a critical differentiation. Table 1 lists 'HiProbeVAD ([Author] et al., 2025)' as a baseline, which is transparently the authors' own prior or concurrent work. SteerVAD's incremental gain over it is the smallest of all comparisons. Without a direct architectural comparison or ablation showing what RSA + HMC adds over the HiProbeVAD mechanism, it is impossible to evaluate whether SteerVAD is a genuinely distinct contribution or an incremental extension of the same line of work.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Provide a technical differentiation section or table comparing the core mechanisms of SteerVAD versus HiProbeVAD, and an ablation that swaps SteerVAD's novel components for the analogous HiProbeVAD components.

key_concerns.issue: Overclaimed performance gap with fine-tuned methods. The abstract and Section 4.2 claim to 'narrow the performance gap with fully-trained fine-tuned methods,' but on XD-Violence the gap to Holmes-VAD is 90.67% − 83.02% = 7.65 pp AP—a large deficit, not a narrow gap. The 'narrowing' framing is misleading.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Revise the framing to accurately reflect the data: competitive with tuning-free approaches while remaining substantially below fine-tuned SOTA on XD-Violence. Do not omit the XD-Violence gap in the discussion.

key_concerns.issue: Two-dataset evaluation is insufficient for the generality claimed. UCF-Crime and XD-Violence are both weakly-supervised benchmarks with surveillance and online video content. Industrial, medical, and traffic anomaly benchmarks (e.g., ShanghaiTech Campus, Avenue, or domain-specific datasets) are absent. The claim that this is 'a powerful new direction for video anomaly detection' broadly is not supported.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one additional VAD benchmark with a distinct domain or annotation protocol (e.g., ShanghaiTech Campus for one-class unsupervised evaluation, or a frame-level industrial benchmark) to assess cross-domain transfer.

key_concerns.issue: RSA's relationship to Fisher's Linear Discriminant / Linear Discriminant Analysis is not acknowledged. The inter-to-intra scatter ratio in Equation (1) is structurally identical to the Fisher criterion (between-class scatter / within-class scatter). The paper presents it as a novel 'gradient-free geometric method' without discussing this connection, which overstates novelty and omits a relevant body of literature.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Acknowledge the Fisher discriminant interpretation, note that the contribution is its application to MLLM attention heads for LAE identification, and discuss why LDA-based selection is more or less appropriate than other methods (e.g., probing classifiers, centered kernel alignment).

key_concerns.issue: Data efficiency analysis (Table 4) is reported only for UCF-Crime. Given that the 1% argument is central to the paper, the same analysis should appear for XD-Violence to confirm it is not dataset-specific.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add the data efficiency table for XD-Violence with equivalent entries.

key_concerns.issue: The post-hoc explainability feature is described in Section 3.5 but never evaluated. No user study, no automatic quality metric (e.g., BLEU, BERTScore relative to ground-truth descriptions), and no qualitative example is provided in the main paper.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either evaluate explainability quality (even a small qualitative study) or remove the feature from the abstract and contributions list, as it is currently an unevaluated design element.

key_concerns.issue: Limitations section is generic boilerplate. It does not name the specific architectural, data-regime, or scale boundaries the authors have in mind, making it uninformative for readers and program chairs.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Replace with concrete limitations: single backbone tested, two datasets, small margins that may not be statistically significant, no evaluation of explainability quality, and sensitivity to the 1% calibration split not demonstrated for XD-Violence.

questions_for_authors: What is the technical relationship between SteerVAD and HiProbeVAD? Can you provide a side-by-side comparison of their mechanisms and an ablation that directly substitutes one component for the other?

The improvement over HiProbeVAD is 0.43 pp AUC on UCF-Crime and 0.87 pp AP on XD-Violence. Given the ±0.04% intra-method variance you report, can you provide a statistical significance test (e.g., bootstrap test on frame-level predictions) confirming these margins are reliable?
The RSA metric in Eq. (1) is structurally the Fisher criterion. Have you compared LAE selection via RSA against standard LDA or probing-classifier-based head selection? Why is Eq. (1) preferable?

The global context vector c is described as 'the final hidden state corresponding to the first generated token'—does this require autoregressive decoding, or is it extracted from a single prefill forward pass? The framework diagram says 'single forward pass' while Section 3.4 implies at least one autoregressive step; please clarify the inference-time cost.

All experiments use InternVL3. Is the RSA-identified set of LAE heads (L18H4, L23H24, L21H21, L22H7) specific to InternVL3's depth/width, or did you observe analogous stable head selection on any other MLLM backbone? Even a preliminary sanity-check result would strengthen the generality claim significantly.
Why is the data efficiency analysis (Table 4) absent for XD-Violence? Does performance on XD-Violence also saturate at 1%, or is the relationship different?
calibration_check: Claims of 'narrowing the gap' with fine-tuned methods are contradicted by a 7.65 pp deficit on XD-Violence; the SOTA-within-tuning-free framing is accurate but the sub-0.9 pp margins over nearest competitors are presented without statistical validation, making the top-line performance claim weaker than the paper suggests.

significance.justification: Tuning-free VAD with 1% calibration data is a practically useful direction, but the marginal gains over the nearest tuning-free baseline and the lack of multi-domain evaluation limit the scope of the demonstrated impact.

novelty.justification: The unified geometric framing (manifold steering, LAE identification, HMC) is a coherent and interesting conceptual contribution, but RSA is structurally Fisher discriminant analysis and the HMC's anisotropic scaling is a form of input-conditioned channel attention—neither component is technically novel in isolation.

rigor.justification: The ablation structure is reasonable and the stability analysis is a genuine strength, but single-backbone evaluation, two-dataset scope, absence of significance tests for small main-table margins, and the unexplained proximity to HiProbeVAD collectively undermine confidence in the conclusions.

statistical_soundness.justification: The main comparison table contains point estimates only; the reported intra-method variance (±0.04%) does not cover cross-method variance, and the sub-1 pp margins over the closest competitor are never subjected to any significance test.

calibration_honesty.justification: The 'narrowing the gap with fine-tuned methods' claim is refuted by a 7.65 pp AP deficit on XD-Violence; the limitations section is generic rather than concrete, and the RSA novelty is overstated relative to Fisher discriminant literature.

clarity.justification: The paper is well-written, the framework description is logically sequenced, and the notation is consistent; minor issues include the ambiguous 'single forward pass' claim and some redundancy between the abstract and introduction.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR structure (Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Methodology, Experiments, Conclusion, Limitations) is followed, with appropriate use of appendices for theoretical and supplementary material.

reproducibility.justification: Hyperparameters, optimizer settings, hardware, and calibration protocol are specified in sufficient detail; the single-backbone constraint and reliance on appendices for topological proofs slightly reduce reproducibility for readers without access to InternVL3 internals.

related_work.justification: Coverage of tuning-free and fine-tuned VAD literature is adequate, but the Fisher/LDA connection to RSA is absent, HiProbeVAD is not differentiated despite being from the same author group, and mechanistic interpretability references are cited without being connected to the specific design choices in HMC.

figure_quality.justification: The t-SNE before/after visualization (Figure 4) and UMAP manifold rendering (Figure 2) are appropriate for the geometric claims; the framework overview (Figure 3) appears comprehensive from its caption, though the conceptual comparison figure (Figure 1) seems to rely on visual layout rather than quantitative differentiation.

breadth_generality.justification: Two benchmarks and one MLLM backbone are wholly insufficient to support claims of a 'powerful new direction for video anomaly detection'; data efficiency analysis is missing for XD-Violence, and no cross-domain or cross-architecture result is provided.

overall_recommendation.justification: An interesting idea with a clean geometric framing and notable data efficiency, but unvalidated margins over the nearest competitor, single-backbone evaluation, two-dataset scope, and a partially overclaimed contribution place this at the borderline-reject threshold without significant additional experiments.
